description: Value-chain segments of the BESS/AIDC ecosystem the Profiler corpus covers, with every covered company assigned to one or more segments in a role. Designed at S0 of INTEGRATED-REMEDIATION-PLAN.md §7 (2026-09-07). Schema: repository-information/PROFILER-SCHEMA.md → 'Segments registry'. Every membership was verified against the company's own dossier — its ecosystemRole and productsAndServices — and the 'basis' field records the line that supports it; the registry category was not used as evidence. The segment lessons (Classroom, generated by scripts/build-classroom-segments.py from S1) and the landscape modules (S2) read this file; the Profiler Command populates it on every new dossier.

roles.incumbent: The dossier places the company in the segment's established leading set — ranked top-tier by a third party, or described by the dossier as the incumbent, the benchmark, the reference, or the leader for what the segment makes or does.
roles.challenger: The dossier places the company as contesting that set — an entrant, a second source, a fast riser, a business converting a base into the segment, a niche or mid-tier player, or a leader elsewhere attacking the market the corpus serves.
roles.adjacent: The segment is not the company's primary business, but its dossier records a product line, a division, a channel, or a buyer or supplier position that touches it. Adjacent members appear in a segment lesson's player table under their own heading and never count toward the floor rule's incumbent or challenger.

tiers.build: builds, powers and cools the plant or the hall
tiers.services: finances, assures, optimises or insures it

floorRule: A landscape module is authored for a segment only when it holds at least three members with a dossier, including at least one incumbent and one challenger (CLASSROOM-CURRICULUM-PLAN.md §10.2). Adjacent members count toward the three but not toward the roles.

segments.name: Cells and chemistry
segments.definition: Makers of the storage cell itself — the lithium-iron-phosphate prismatic cell that every containerized system is built from, the high-power NCA/LMO and lead-carbon cells under UPS and BBU duty, and the non-lithium chemistries (sodium-ion, iron-air) contesting the long end. The first link in the value chain: every integrator, UPS maker and BBU shelf below it buys or makes a cell here.
buyingCriteria: Cycle life and calendar life against the warranty curve
Cost per kWh at the cell and the format (Ah class) that sets container count
Chemistry fit to duty — energy vs power cell, C-rate, cold performance
Prohibited-foreign-entity status and the factory's location (status follows ownership, not site)
Factory capacity and delivery slots; yield record
Safety certification (UL 9540A at cell level) and the fire record
segments.notes: Reserved adjacent role for upstream materials (lithium, LFP cathode, graphite/anode), which join here as adjacent members rather than as a segment of their own (INTEGRATED-REMEDIATION-PLAN.md §7.2). PARTLY FILLED at S3 P5 (2026-09-09, v05.28r): albemarle joined on lithium and novonix on synthetic graphite anode material, both adjacent. Still reserved for the private cathode and cell names of E4b/E6b — mitra-chem and cornex. Note that the two public alternates named in the original plan are no longer interchangeable: ICL discontinued its US LFP cathode project on 2025-11-11 so the premise is dead, and Syrah is pre-commercial at Vidalia with a going-concern flag; westwater-resources is the clean graphite alternate. Both members added here are pre-cell suppliers and neither counts toward the floor's incumbent or challenger requirement. S3 P6 (2026-09-09, v05.29r) added calb and great-power, both CHALLENGER on the SNE H1-2026 storage-cell ranking (CALB 5th at 31.5 GWh / 6.8%; Great Power 10th at 20.5 GWh / 4.4%, +202%). Neither could be typed incumbent: this segment's incumbent bar is top-three plus explicit leader language, and EVE Energy is typed challenger at 2nd and 10.4%. EVE/HITHIUM TENSION EXAMINED AND DISMISSED (2026-09-09, v05.31r, non-session pass): P6 flagged that on the SNE H1-2026 table EVE ranks 2nd (48.0 GWh) as a challenger while hithium ranks 3rd (46.2 GWh) as an incumbent, and correctly left it alone. Reading both ecosystemRole fields resolves it as a FALSE POSITIVE rather than a mistyping, and NEITHER ROLE WAS CHANGED. The two roles rest on different axes and different evidence, not on one table. hithium's basis is multi-house and full-year - No. 3 in 2024 (35.1 GWh, ~11%) and Top 2 in both total and utility-scale ESS shipments for 2025 on InfoLink, SMM and ICC, with cumulative shipments past 100 GWh - which is top-three plus explicit leader language, the segment's incumbent bar, and which places it ABOVE EVE on its own sources. EVE's dossier does not claim the leader position at all: it assesses EVE as 'the aggressive-challenger cell supplier ... the vendor forcing the 600Ah+ transition', which is the challenger definition stated verbatim. The apparent inversion is an artifact of comparing one house's half-year table against another's full-year one across a 1.8 GWh gap (~4%) that reverses between houses and periods. THE LESSON FOR THE S2 LANDSCAPE AUTHOR: rank order on any single table is not the role test, and a future session should not 're-type' either company on the strength of the SNE row alone. The SNE H1-2026 top twelve is now ELEVEN of twelve covered; the twelfth is cornex at 7th, ranked ABOVE both companies added here, and it is a private E6b/V4 subject.

The §8 row allowed Supermicro to be either incumbent or challenger; the record decided challenger. Dell and HPE, the named alternates, were not needed and remain uncovered — the segment still has no dossier for the two largest OEM competitors, and no ODM (Foxconn, Quanta, Wiwynn) is covered even though ODM Direct is now above 50% of the server market.

segments.notes: Started at zero (INTEGRATED-REMEDIATION-PLAN.md §7.2). S3 V1 (2026-09-08, v05.21r) landed kWh Analytics as the challenger; S3 P2 (2026-09-09) landed Marsh McLennan and Aon as the two incumbents, taking the segment to 3 members / 2 incumbents / 1 challenger — AT THE FLOOR. Two caveats recorded at assignment. (1) The challenger's independence is being overtaken by events: kWh agreed in March 2026 to be acquired by Beazley, which is itself being acquired by Zurich for USD 10.9bn with completion expected in the second half of 2026, so 'challenger' may be the wrong label by the end of 2026 and the role should be re-read at the first refresh. (2) The two incumbents are not equals — Marsh McLennan is about USD 9.8bn larger on total revenue and has been first for sixteen consecutive years, while Aon leads on data-centre capacity and on FY2025 organic growth (6 percent against 4 percent) and is buying USI for USD 17.0bn, which takes its leverage to about 4.8x. A finding that spans both incumbents and belongs to this segment rather than to either dossier: neither broker anchors its battery-storage guidance to a named standard. Across seven Marsh documents and every Aon battery and renewables publication reviewed, no UL 9540A, NFPA 855, DNV, CSA, TUV or IEC reference appears; both state insurer requirements in engineering terms and leave the code unnamed. That is the gap the assurance segment's members occupy. The bankability guidance module carries insurers and brokers as Moss Landing pricing context only (curriculum plan §6, G10).
